window.title: Which CVEs Vedette reports
window.description: CVEs published in the last 12 months, and older ones only while they are exploited in the wild.
window.descriptionInfo: By default Vedette reports, and keeps the data of, the CVEs published in the last 12 months, and an older CVE only while there is evidence of exploitation in the wild: an exploited list (CISA KEV, VulnCheck KEV, your own lists) or a vendor saying it is exploited. Old flaws on those lists are what attackers use most, so they never age out. A public exploit (Exploit-DB, Metasploit, a proof of concept) keeps an older CVE only when it came out in the last 12 months, and this network's own intrusion alerts keep a CVE they name for 12 months after the latest one. Older CVEs without any of that are not findings or questions.
window.offHelp: Off (the default). Switch it on to report every CVE, also old ones nobody is known to exploit.
window.onHelp: On: every CVE NVD and the CVE Program publish is reported, whatever its age. The vulnerability data is about 2.5 times larger (about 0.9 GB instead of about 0.35 GB).
window.onBody: Vedette keeps every CVE instead of those of the last 12 months and the exploited ones: about 2.5 times as many, about 0.9 GB of data instead of about 0.35 GB. Over the next hours the box reads NVD's whole list (about 165 requests, about 200 MB) and the CVE Program's whole list (about 670 MB) once more, from the same addresses as now. Older CVEs on your devices then become findings and questions too.
window.offTitle: Report only the last 12 months and exploited CVEs?
window.offBody: At the next match, open findings of older CVEs that are not exploited in the wild close as outside the reporting window, and their questions go away. Nothing is deleted: a finding opens again if you switch this back on or its CVE becomes exploited. Findings a safe check proved or a person confirmed stay open. The older CVEs leave the data at the next check.
window.nowOn: CVEs of every age are reported. The older ones arrive over the next hours.
window.nowOff: Only CVEs of the last 12 months and exploited ones are reported.

parser.title: How Vedette reads this feed
parser.intro: Choose the format, map each field, then test on a sample.
parser.introInfo: Choose the format, say where each field is, then test on a sample. Rows that do not fit are counted and skipped, never crash the fetch.
parser.recordsInfo: The JSONPath to the list of records. Supported: .key, ['key'], [n], [*].

note.json: Each record is mapped with a JSONPath relative to it, such as {{example}}.
note.csv: Name a column from the header, or give its number.
note.rss: Use item fields: title, link, description, pubDate (or published), category, id.
note.stix: Indicator objects are read; fields are fixed, nothing to map.
note.lines: One indicator per line; its kind is detected.

noteInfo.csv: Lines starting with # are skipped. Name a column from the header, or give its number.
noteInfo.stix: Vedette reads indicator objects and their patterns, such as [ipv4-addr:value = '203.0.113.7'], [domain-name:value = '...'], [url:value = '...'] and file hashes. A bundle or a TAXII collection response both work. Fields are fixed; nothing to map.
noteInfo.lines: One indicator per line; blank lines and # comments are skipped. Only the first word on each line is used. The kind (IP, domain, URL, hash) is detected.

parser.srcCsv: Column name or number. Empty = not mapped.
